text:
alice: quick q — hitting a schema/typing mismatch when invoking an action via the Ruby SDK in streaming mode. The stream parses but some numeric fields come through as strings on partial chunks. cc @morgan @ben

morgan: can you paste an example of expected vs observed?

alice: sure — simplified example. expected full object after the call finishes:
```json
{"user": {"id": 123, "active": true, "email": "a@b.com"}}
```
observed on early streaming chunks we see:
```json
{"user": {"id": "123", "active": "true", "email": "a@b.com"}}
```
so ints/bools get stringified when the chunk boundaries hit those tokens. Parser eventually yields correct types once message completes, but our SDK helper that coerces to typed structs runs per-chunk currently and picks up wrong types.

ben: ah yeah, that's nasty. we've historically run lightweight coercion on each chunk to support partial structured outputs, but it makes assumptions about token boundaries. Two quick mitigations: 1) only run coercion when the chunk is a complete JSON object (detect closed braces), or 2) provide an opt-in `coerce_full_message: true` so apps can wait until final.

ben: example ruby shim idea:
```ruby
client.invoke_action(payload, stream: true, coerce_mode: :final_only) do |chunk, meta|
  if chunk.complete_json? || config.coerce_mode == :per_chunk
    safe = SDK::TypeCoercer.coerce(chunk.json, schema)
    yield safe, meta
  else
    yield chunk, meta
  end
end
```

zane: fwiw we also saw auth/retry weirdness with streaming — if the server returns a 401 mid-stream the retry logic triggers a full reconnect and the SDK replays from start, but the app-level idempotency isn't guaranteed. That replay interacts poorly with streaming type coercion because you may see partial stringified values then final ones after retry.

ravi: suggestion: add a separate retry policy for streaming calls (no automatic retries on auth errors, surface them as terminal unless the app explicitly opts into replay). Also expose a `buffer_until_complete: true/false` option so higher-level clients can choose to accumulate full objects before coercion.

devex-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ruby/pull/412 — adds `coerce_mode` + `buffer_until_complete` flags and a small test vector for partial-chunk numeric coercion :eyes:

alice: nice, I'll try the branch. If we need a small RFC I'll draft one describing the tradeoffs (latency vs correctness) and propose default = no per-chunk coercion.

morgan: +1 on RFC. Defaulting to safer behaviour makes sense; customers who want ultra-low-latency partial structs can opt in. Also add a note in the auth docs about streaming retries; we should recommend using short-lived tokens + reconnect hooks.

ben: quick code-review ping when ready — I'm happy to pair on the test harness for partial-fragmented JSON. :thumbsup:

azane: minor nit — name the option `coerce_streaming_mode` so it's explicit in logs.

alice: thanks all — updating PR with a test case showing integer->string fragmentation and adding a small section in the Ruby README. I'll link back here when done. :rocket:
